angle: Pastoral: presence over problem-solving. Someone opens this at 2am after a diagnosis, a death, a marriage cracking, or a night they don't want to survive. The app's job is to be there, put words in front of them they don't have to earn, and — if it's that bad — put a real human and a real number one tap away without making them go looking. Everything that measures, counts, congratulates, sells, or asks them to commit is removed, because all of it says "perform" to a person who can't.
thesis: The comfort path is already right in spirit and the research says so — "just the scriptures, nothing asked, no graduation prompt" (PERSONA-RESEARCH-2026-09-10.md, Persona 6, Journey). So this is not a rebuild. It is four additions and six subtractions. Add: a persistent one-tap comfort door in the seam that opens a calm full-screen surface from any path and never touches the saved path ("Crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day"); region-correct crisis lines that never default to 988; a private human next step to a real campus pastor that does not go on the public prayer wall; and a co-created "When it's bad" card, Wysa's most-used feature at over 49% of crisis users. Subtract everything on the current comfort screen that counts or congratulates — "Reading {x} of {y}", "You're doing great.", the day-two ask to commit to a daily quota, the completion-framed "I've finished reading" — because the research is explicit: "no streak, no count, no 'complete'", and guilt-framed nudges drive opt-out and uninstall. The locked look wins over the research's "dark and calm": low stimulus here means fewer moving parts on the warm ivory canvas, not a dark theme.
principles: Nothing is asked. No count, no streak, no completion, no graduation — ever. (Research Persona 6 delivery line; ruling: 'Feeling Stronger?' removed for good.)

Presence before explanation. Verses that say God is near, not verses that explain why this happened. Romans 8:28 and Jeremiah 29:11 are explanation verses and are excluded from the crisis surface. (Pargament 2004: negative religious coping — 'have more faith' — predicts decline.)
Crisis is reachable from a good day's screen. One persistent tap from every path, opening comfort without switching the saved path.
Never show the wrong country's number. Resolve region or ask — never default. (Crisis journal 2021: some apps show the wrong country's hotline.)

Resources, not disclaimers. One short honest line that leads to the number, not a liability wall. (81% of mental-health apps carry disclaimers instead of resources; only 35% show crisis resources in-app.)
A cry for help is never blocked, never gated, never public. The message sends; the confirm appears beside it. No email gate in front of it. Not on the prayer wall.
Slow audio first. Someone in crisis often cannot read. (Research Persona 6, delivery.)
The human next step is a real person at their campus, with no promised response time we can't keep at 2am.
Low stimulus inside the locked look: fewer elements, more air, ivory canvas, white paper panel, upright Georgia. Never dark, never stripped.
Nothing they type is ever stored in an analytics event.

journey.day0: They are not on the comfort path. Something happens. They open Daily Word on their usual path — congregation, or new_to_faith, or nothing at all — and the word Comfort sits quietly in the seam at the top of every screen where it has always been. One tap opens Comfort Now full-screen. The saved path is untouched, no plan day is credited, nothing is stamped. When they close it, they are exactly where they were. This is the day the research means by 'Crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day.'
journey.first_session: Comfort Now, or the comfort path if they chose it in the sheet. One line: nothing is asked of you here. One presence verse on the white paper panel, large and upright. Listen sits above the passage as the primary control, because reading may be beyond them. One chapter, already loaded, no translation pills at the top, no counter. Under it: keep this verse, a different one, talk to someone. At the foot, one honest line and a link to who to call. Nothing is asked. Nothing is offered for tomorrow. No push prompt (comfort is already excluded from PushOptIn — keep it). No asked-once path screen (already excluded — keep it). The streak records silently and is never shown.
journey.return_visit: Same surface, a new presence verse by local day index, the next comfort chapter. If they kept a verse yesterday, the When it's bad card now has one of its three slots filled and shows quietly below the chapter — no prompt to complete it. At the end of this second session, and only this one, one line: want one quiet check-in tomorrow. Yes, once. Or no. That is the entire ask of the first week.
journey.week2: On the third distinct day they come back, one quiet line under the done card: want more than one chapter ready each day. One, two, three, or just one is fine. Answered once, never asked again. By week two the When it's bad card is usually one or two slots filled, built by taps they chose, never by a form we put in front of them. The pastoral message, if they sent one, has been read by a person at their campus. There is still no streak, no count, no graduation prompt, and no invitation to move to another path. They leave comfort only by choosing it in the path sheet.
journey.missed_day: Nothing happens. No catch-up, no 'we missed you', no broken-streak repair prompt, no recovery copy. The single check-in they opted into fires once and does not repeat. This is the deliberate answer to the cross-cutting finding that guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall — a person in a hard season is the one reader for whom that risk is highest and the upside is lowest.
journey.seasonal: Comfort is the one path that gets no seasonal campaign. The calendar-moment finding (3M one-year-plan starts on 1 Jan, 21.6M Easter opens, Hallow's Lent spike) is about the movable middle, not about someone in crisis. The only seasonal behaviour: between 20 December and 2 January, and on any date the person has marked on their When it's bad card, the verse banner draws from presence-tagged verses only. No count, no invitation, no banner announcing it.

comfort_access: One persistent tap, in the seam strip that already sits above every screen on every path (Seam.tsx, mounted at App.tsx:458). Label: the word Comfort with a heart outline, muted weight, aria-label 'Open comfort now'. It opens ComfortNow full-screen via useSubView alone, mounted with a live open prop — never conditionally mounted, never useSubView plus useModalA11y, per both nested-overlay rulings. It writes nothing: no saveSetup, no dw_setup stamp, no dw_path_asked, no plan-day credit, no handleRead. Close returns to the exact screen and scroll position. This is the direct answer to the research line 'From every path: a persistent one-tap I need comfort now that opens comfort without switching the saved path. Crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day.' A sixth tab was rejected — the tab bar is already five and a Crisis tab labels the person every day of their life. Two gaps to name: the seam is hidden when IS_EMBEDDED, so the futures.church iframe embed has no door (owner decision), and someone who uses the door but never switches path should still keep Who to call and When it's bad in Settings — designed above.
reminders: Comfort's reminder policy is almost entirely subtraction, because the cross-cutting finding is that streaks work until they shame and guilt-framed reminders drive opt-out and uninstall — and a person in a hard season is the reader for whom that risk is highest and the upside lowest. So: comfort stays excluded from the generic full-screen PushOptIn (App.tsx:312, keep). There is no daily comfort reminder. There is no missed-day catch-up, no streak repair prompt, no 'we missed you'. The streak is recorded silently on mount and never displayed (HomeScreen.tsx:2004-2006, keep) so that it survives if they later move to another path. The single reminder in the whole design is one opt-in, one-shot check-in offered at the end of the second session only — 'Want one quiet check-in tomorrow?' / 'Yes, once' — firing once, at the hour they used the app today, with copy that mentions no streak and no count: 'Still here.' / 'The same verse, or a new one.' A recurring reminder exists only if the person sets a daily chapter amount, which is itself only offered on the third distinct day and never re-asked. And there is no graduation prompt of any kind, at any interval, forever: UPGRADE_CONDITIONS has no comfort row and pathway-upgrades.test.ts:25-27 locks it — that test must be extended to cover the new surfaces so no future card re-opens the door.
instrumentation: comfort_open, with from = seam | home | push | path — proves whether the from-everywhere tap actually gets reach from other paths, the research's own named test ('Comfort-tap reach from other paths').
comfort_passage_read and comfort_listen — whether audio-first is what a crisis reader actually takes, which the research asserts but does not source.
comfort_verse_kept and comfort_card_filled (slot = call | steadies | verse) — whether the When it's bad card gets built by taps, against Wysa's 49%-of-crisis-users benchmark.
comfort_pastor_sent, and comfort_pastor_sent_no_email — whether removing the email gate changes send rate at all.
comfort_safety_shown, with trigger = link | ai | prayer — the safety-flow trigger rate.

comfort_safety_answered, with answer = safe | not_safe — the false-positive rate, the research's second named test. A high 'safe' share means the phrase list is too broad and needs narrowing, not celebrating.
comfort_line_tapped, with region — proves the region resolver is showing the right country, and surfaces any region that is being served the picker instead of a number.
comfort_checkin_optin and comfort_checkin_opened — whether the one-shot check-in is wanted, and whether it earns the exception to the no-push-for-comfort rule.

comfort_return_d1 / _d7 / _d30 by path, via the nightly rollup the research puts first in build order — 'Only the app's own instrumentation can answer these. That is the single biggest gap and the first build.' Specifically: next-day return after a comfort session, the research's third named test.

TRAP: src/utils/analytics.ts:24-31 TRACKED_EVENTS is an allowlist. An event name not in that array is dropped silently — the dashboard will show a clean zero and look like the feature is unused. Every name above must be added there in the same PR.

PRIVACY: none of these carry the text of what the person wrote or typed. comfort_safety_shown records that it fired and which trigger, never the phrase. comfort_card_filled records which slot, never its contents. The phone number on the When it's bad card is the most sensitive thing this app will ever hold and it never reaches an event.
self_serve_levers: src/data/comfort.ts — COMFORT_CHAPTERS and COMFORT_DEVOTIONS are already plain data a campus pastor can edit. Extend each entry with tone: 'presence' | 'explanation' so the crisis surface can draw from presence only.

MOVE COMFORT_VERSES and GUIDED_PRAYERS out of src/sections/ComfortVerseBannerSection.tsx:13-37 into src/data/comfort.ts. They are the most-edited comfort content in the app and they currently sit inside a render file, which makes every wording change a component edit.
src/data/crisis-lines.ts (new) — region → [{name, number, tel, note}]. The one file a campus pastor in Bali or Rio must own. Adding a nation is a data row, not a code change.
src/data/crisis-terms.ts (new) — the flag phrase list, per language, extendable without touching BibleAI.tsx.

dw_comfort_daily — the reader's own lever, already live, already synced via syncMisc.
ChoosePathSheet / the Home path swatch — the only way in or out of the comfort path. The reader leaves by choosing, never by a prompt.

STILL NEEDS A DEVELOPER, and say so honestly: sectionOrder for comfort (persona-config.ts), the phrase-check threshold, push templates in netlify/functions/push-send.js, and the analytics allowlist. None of these have an admin UI and none should acquire one for this build.

open_decisions: Does comfort get the one-shot next-day check-in at all? It crosses your standing line that comfort never gets push (App.tsx:312). The research calls it 'plausible, unsourced, worth testing.' Designed here as opt-in, offered once, fired once, never recurring — but it is your call whether comfort gets a notification of any kind.

The Indonesian and Brazilian crisis lines, and the Futuros question: does a Spanish-speaking reader in Georgia get 988 in Spanish, or a Spanish-language line? I have not invented numbers for Indonesia or Brazil and will not. Until you fill them, those regions see the honest 'we don't have a number for your country yet' line plus the pastor route. The research names this as yours: 'The crisis lines to show per congregation.'

Who at each campus receives a pastoral request, and what we promise. I have written 'Someone from {campus} will see it' with no response time, because at 2am we cannot keep one. If a campus can commit to a window, say so and I will put it in the copy. The research names this as yours too.
Does the pastoral request send without an email address? I have designed it to — an email gate in front of a cry for help is indefensible, and it departs from the prayer-wall pattern. Confirm.

Do Romans 8:28 and Jeremiah 29:11 stay in the general comfort verse rotation? They are excluded from the crisis surface either way. In acute grief these two are the verses most often experienced as dismissal rather than comfort.

Is the comfort door in the seam visible to every persona from day one, or only after someone has used comfort once? Day one is my recommendation — the whole point is that it is already there before it is needed — but it puts a word about crisis on a pastor's and a new believer's screen every day.
The seam is hidden when IS_EMBEDDED, so the futures.church iframe embed of Daily Word would have no comfort door. Add one there, or accept the gap?

Does dw_comfort_card sync to the cloud at all? It will hold a phone number — the most sensitive thing this app stores. Default in this design: yes, through misc, fill-only, tombstoned deletes. Say if you want it device-only.
risks: Showing the wrong country's number. The worst failure mode in the whole design, and the exact failure the research names. Mitigation: never default; campus region first, geo second, locale third, picker fourth. A wrong number is worse than no number.

A false-positive safety confirm reading as surveillance — someone types 'I'm dying of embarrassment' and the app asks if they are safe. Mitigation: never block the message, one-tap dismiss, never re-fire in the same conversation, and measure the safe/not_safe ratio as the tuning signal rather than the success metric.

Creating a duty of care the campus cannot staff. 'Talk to someone' at 2am with no one reading until Tuesday is worse than not offering it. Mitigation: the copy promises a reader, never a time; and the crisis lines sit under the form, always.
Anything from this leaking to the public prayer wall. Separate table, separate function, and a check that specifically confirms nothing appears on the wall.
The push exception re-opening the shame door. One check-in becomes a daily one becomes a streak nudge in six months. Mitigation: one-shot by construction, and the template carries no count.

Translation. Comfort devotional translations ride your existing waiver; crisis lines and the AI flag phrases do NOT — those are safety content and need your sign-off per language. A mistranslated safety prompt is worse than none, so the confirm does not fire for a language whose list is unapproved.
Preview gate. Both the seam door and the comfort sectionOrder change are visible on the opening screen. Neither merges without your look at the deploy preview.

dw_comfort_card riding in the misc JSONB column with a phone number in it. applyMisc is fill-only and deletes are tombstones, per your rulings, but this is the first genuinely sensitive record the app has held.

build_steps.step: 1. Instrumentation first, as the research orders it. Add every comfort_* event to the allowlist and a small typed helper.
build_steps.check: npx vitest run with a new spec asserting each comfort_* name in comfort-events.ts is present in TRACKED_EVENTS. A name missing from the allowlist is dropped silently and the dashboard shows a clean zero.

build_steps.step: 2. Crisis lines data and the region resolver. Campus region first, geo second, locale third, picker fourth — no default.
build_steps.check: npx vitest run: AU campus resolves to 13 11 14, US campus to 988, an Indonesian campus to the no-number-yet state, and an unresolved user to the picker. Assert explicitly that no input path returns 988 as a fallback.

build_steps.step: 3. The Who to call sheet. New CSS prefix dw-cmf-* (dw-cp-* is ChoosePathSheet, dw-path-* is the Plans chooser).
build_steps.check: npm run build, then open it on a preview from Settings with a US campus and again with an AU campus and read the numbers off the screen.

build_steps.step: 4. The seam comfort door and the Comfort Now surface. useSubView alone, mounted with a live open prop.
build_steps.check: npm run build, then in preview: snapshot localStorage.dw_setup, open Comfort Now from a congregation persona, close it, and assert dw_setup and dw_reading_done are byte-identical. Then press Android back from inside it and confirm one history entry pops, not two.

build_steps.step: 5. Move comfort content into data and tag it presence/explanation.
build_steps.files: src/data/comfort.ts (add COMFORT_VERSES, GUIDED_PRAYERS, tone tags); src/sections/ComfortVerseBannerSection.tsx (import instead of declare)
build_steps.check: npx tsc -b, plus a test that fixes the local date and asserts the chosen verse and chapter are identical before and after the move — the localDayIndex invariant must not shift by a single day.

build_steps.step: 6. Rework the ComfortSection post-read: drop the counter, replace the finish button with the thought offer, collapse three steps to two exits, relocate the daily-amount ask to day three.
build_steps.check: npx vitest run: assert comfort_reading_x_of_y never renders, that no ask_lock fires in sessions one or two, and that the two exits both reach the done state. Then npm run build and walk it in preview with the persona-testing recipe in CLAUDE.md.

build_steps.step: 7. Talk to someone — a private route that is not the prayer wall.
build_steps.files: src/components/ReachPastor.tsx (new); netlify/functions/pastoral-request.js (new); supabase/migrations/<ts>_pastoral_requests.sql (new, in the repo per the standing rule); src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx (mount)
